review.reason: The actual source CH and RoW producer documentation and the native service-station documentation identify the same initial medium-pressure network boundary (0.1–1bar), electricity requirements and gas-loss emissions. This pressure is the inlet boundary; it does not establish the final vehicle delivery pressure. Both products reference+1kg. Use factor+1 per signed kg; do not add compression, assume a final pressure, or infer an energy/density factor. Source global market shares are approximately99.1583%RoW and0.8417%CH, with no market freight or losses. Replace that market once by the complete native CH service station as a geographic screening proxy. Source CH station electricity and infrastructure draws match the native values; upstream gas supply, regional sourcing, LHV metadata and vintage differ. Source metadata contains conflicting46.5/48.98MJ/kg statements; native upstream fuel is MJ-based internally. Do not reinterpret the caller kg as MJ or normalize these inventories by an assumed heating value. Preserve signed caller quantities, formulas, supported uncertainty, separate freight and emissions. Retain the complete installed native inventory once, including its background, geography, allocation and vintage. This is an explicitly limited screening correspondence; score effects are unquantified and LCIA equivalence or impact completeness is not established. Only inspected ecoinvent3.9cutoff is added; no inverse, cross-system-model or other-release approval is inferred.
